segments.text: Τρίτῃ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ, ὥσπερ ὁ Σωσίας προεῖπεν, ὁ ἄγγελος ἀνέζευξεν.
Ὁ γὰρ Σωσίας τὸν ἵππον αὐτοῦ καλῶς ἐθεράπευσεν, καὶ νῦν τοῖς τέτταρσι ποσὶν ὀρθῶς ἔβαινεν.

pins.note: Attic ττ; agrees with ποσίν.

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Ξενοφῶν τῷ ἀγγέλῳ ἐπιστολὴν ἔδωκε πρὸς τὸν Σοφαίνετον.
«Τί ἔγραψας, ὦ πάτερ;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.

pins.note: Vocative particle, not a subjunctive of εἰμί.

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ὅπερ ἐπηγγειλάμην,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «“Ὁ χειμὼν χειμὼν ἦν.”»

pins.note: Canonical course lexeme grc-epaggellomai: promise.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Μόνον τοῦτο;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Μόνον τοῦτο,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «τὰ δὲ ἄλλα ὑμῖν λέξω, οὐ τῷ Σοφαινέτῳ.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: Ἑσπέρας δὲ πάντες πάλιν παρὰ τῷ πυρὶ ἦσαν, ὁ δὲ Σωσίας ἐν τῇ θύρᾳ ἔστη.

inference_aids.alt: Evening indoors at Scillus: Xenophon tells the story by the hearth, the two boys listen on a bench, and Sosias stands in the doorway looking doubtful.
inference_aids.art_brief: Frame story, Scillus, a spring evening about 384 BC, inside the plain farmhouse. A low hearth fire gives warm light. Xenophon (about 45, short greying beard, oatmeal tunic, dark green cloak) sits by the fire, one hand raised as he tells a story. Gryllus (12, madder-red tunic) and Diodorus (10, woad-blue tunic, chestnut curls) sit side by side on a wooden bench, Diodorus leaning forward. Philesia (dark hair, cream peplos, ochre mantle) sits a little apart with a spindle. Sosias (old Thracian, grey beard, fox-skin cap, zigzag-banded cloak) stands in the open doorway with arms folded and a sceptical face. Painterly, consistent with the visual bible; no lettering, no vase pastiche.

pins.note: Intransitive root aorist: stood.

segments.text: «Ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος· «ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐκάθευδον.»

pins.note: Morpheus compound index κατά-καθεύδω; canonical καθεύδω, imperfect first singular.

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐγὼ δὲ πάντα ἤκουσα,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Τί οὖν ἤκουσας;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «“Δαρείου καὶ Παρυσάτιδος γίγνονται παῖδες δύο,”» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος, «καὶ ἔπειτα οὐδέν.»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Ξενοφῶν ἐγέλασε καὶ ἤρξατο.
«Ὁ Δαρεῖος βασιλεὺς ἦν τῶν Περσῶν, καὶ δύο παῖδες αὐτῷ καὶ τῇ Παρυσάτιδι ἦσαν· πρεσβύτερος μὲν Ἀρταξέρξης, νεώτερος δὲ Κῦρος.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ Κῦρος, ὁ τῶν παίδων βασιλεύς;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Οὔ· ἄλλος Κῦρος, πολλοῖς ἔτεσιν ὕστερον,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐγὼ μὲν πρεσβύτερος, σὺ δὲ νεώτερος,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφόν.
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Ὁ δὲ Δαρεῖος γέρων ἦν καὶ ἠσθένει,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.

inference_aids.gloss: ἀσθενεῖν ↔ ἰσχυρὸν εἶναι

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐνόσει οὖν;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐνόσει,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν, «καὶ ὑπώπτευε τελευτὴν τοῦ βίου· ἐβούλετο οὖν ἀμφοτέρους τοὺς παῖδας παρεῖναι.»

inference_aids.gloss: τελευτὴ τοῦ βίου = θάνατος

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ μὲν οὖν Ἀρταξέρξης ἤδη παρῆν· τὸν δὲ Κῦρον ἐκ τῆς ἀρχῆς μετεπέμψατο.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐκ τῆς ἀρχῆς;» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος· «καὶ σὺ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀρχῆς λέγεις.»
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἄλλη ἀρχή,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «ἀρχὴ γάρ ἐστι καὶ ἡ χώρα ἧς ὁ σατράπης ἄρχει.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ τὸν Κῦρον σατράπην ἐποίησε καὶ στρατηγὸν ἔταξεν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἀνέβη οὖν ὁ Κῦρος πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἀσθενοῦντα, καὶ ὁ Τισσαφέρνης αὐτῷ ἠκολούθει· ὁ γὰρ Κῦρος τῇ φιλίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἐπίστευεν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐπεὶ δὲ ὁ Δαρεῖος ἐτελεύτησε, βασιλεὺς ἐγένετο ὁ Ἀρταξέρξης.»

inference_aids.alt: Family tree: Darius and Parysatis at the top; below them their two sons, Artaxerxes the elder, who became king, and Cyrus the younger, satrap.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ δὲ Τισσαφέρνης τὸν Κῦρον πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν διέβαλεν.»

inference_aids.gloss: διέβαλεν ← διαβάλλω (βάλλω, ἔβαλον): ψευδῆ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Διέβαλεν;» ἤρετο ὁ Γρύλλος· «τί ἔβαλεν; ἀκόντιον;»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Οὐκ ἀκόντιον, ἀλλὰ λόγους,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «ἔλεγε γὰρ ὅτι ὁ Κῦρος τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἐπιβουλεύοι.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἐπιβουλεύειν τινί: βουλεύεσθαι ὅπως τινὰ κακῶς ποιήσει

pins.note: Oblique optative.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἀχάριστος γὰρ ἦν ὁ Τισσαφέρνης,» ἔφη ὁ Σωσίας, «καὶ ἀεὶ πάντας διέβαλλεν.»
segments.speaker: char-sosias

segments.text: «Ὁ δὲ βασιλεὺς ἐπίστευσεν;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐπίστευσε, καὶ τὸν Κῦρον συνέλαβεν,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «ἀποκτεῖναι γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐβούλετο.»

inference_aids.gloss: συνέλαβεν ← συλλαμβάνω (λαμβάνω, ἔλαβον): νῦν συλλαμβάνει, τότε συνέλαβεν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τὸν ἀδελφόν;» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος, καὶ πρὸς τὸν Γρύλλον ἔβλεψεν.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἡ δὲ μήτηρ,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν, «αὐτὸν ἐξῃτήσατο, καὶ πάλιν εἰς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἀπέπεμψεν.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἐξαιτεῖσθαί τινα: τὸν βασιλέα αἰτεῖν μὴ ἀποκτεῖναι αὐτόν
inference_aids.reveal_en: begged him off, won his release

pins.note: Canonical grc-exaiteomai: beg off / obtain release.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: Ὁ δὲ Διόδωρος πρὸς τὴν μητέρα ἔβλεψεν, ἡ δὲ Φιλησία οὐδὲν εἶπεν.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Εἰκός,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «καὶ ὁ Κῦρος ὠργίζετο, καὶ τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἐχαλέπαινεν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐβουλεύετο οὖν ὅπως μήποτε ἔτι ὑπὸ τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἔσται, ἀλλ’ αὐτὸς ἀντ’ ἐκείνου βασιλεύσει.»

pins.note: Morpheus mp category; semantically middle: deliberated / planned.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐπεβούλευεν οὖν τῷ ἀδελφῷ;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος· «ἀληθῆ οὖν ἔλεγεν ὁ Τισσαφέρνης;»
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Τότε μὲν ψευδῆ,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν, «ὕστερον δὲ ἀληθῆ.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἀλλ’ οὐ δίκαιον ἦν,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος· «ὁ γὰρ Ἀρταξέρξης πρεσβύτερος ἦν καὶ ἤδη βασιλεύς.»
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Πῶς ἐτόλμησεν ὁ νεώτερος ἐπὶ τὸν βασιλέα στρατεύειν;»

inference_aids.gloss: στρατεύειν ἐπί τινα: στράτευμα ἐπί τινα ἄγειν

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ὀρθῶς λέγει,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος· «ὁ γὰρ πρεσβύτερος ἀεὶ ἄρχει.»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Οὐ τοῦτο λέγω,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ὁμολογῶ,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «ὁ Κῦρος τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἐπεβούλευσεν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Σκόπει δὲ τί ἔπαθεν· πρῶτον μὲν διεβλήθη, ἔπειτα συνελήφθη, ἔπειτα δὲ ἠτιμάσθη.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἔπαθεν ← πάσχω (ἔπαθον): νῦν πάσχει, τότε ἔπαθεν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἡ δὲ μήτηρ τὸν Κῦρον μᾶλλον φίλον εἶχεν ἢ τὸν βασιλεύοντα, καὶ αὐτῷ ἀεὶ εὔνους ἦν.»

inference_aids.gloss: εὔνους ← εὖ + νοῦς: ἀγαθὰ βουλόμενός τινι

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ταῦτα οὖν πάντα τὸν Κῦρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἤγαγεν.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Λῷον ἦν αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἀρχῇ μένειν,» ἔφη ὁ Διόδωρος.

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐγὼ μὲν τὸν Τισσαφέρνην αἰτιῶμαι,» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος· «ἐκεῖνος γὰρ πρῶτος διέβαλεν.»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Τίς οὖν ὑπαίτιος ἦν,» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος, «ὁ Κῦρος ἢ ὁ Τισσαφέρνης;»
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Δύο ἀδελφοί,» ἔφη ἡ Φιλησία, «καὶ μήτηρ ᾗ ὁ ἕτερος μᾶλλον φίλος ἦν.»
segments.speaker: char-philesia

segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Οὐκ εὐθύς,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «πρῶτον γὰρ στράτευμα ἤθροιζε, καὶ τὴν παρασκευὴν ἔκρυπτεν, ὅπως ὁ βασιλεὺς μὴ αἴσθοιτο.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἀθροίζειν: πολλοὺς εἰς ἓν ἄγειν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τὴν δὲ γνώμην ὀλίγοις ἀνεκοίνου.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τοὺς δὲ παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως ἥκοντας οὕτως εὐηργέτει ὥστε αὐτῷ εὔνους εἶναι μᾶλλον ἢ τῷ βασιλεῖ.»

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Καὶ τῶν βαρβάρων τῶν παρ’ ἑαυτῷ πολλὴν ἐπιμέλειαν ἐποιεῖτο.»
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Καὶ ἡμᾶς ταῖς εὐεργεσίαις εὔνους ἐποίει,» ἔφη ὁ Σωσίας.
segments.speaker: char-sosias

segments.text: «Ἐν δὲ ταῖς πόλεσιν,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν, «ἦσαν φρούραρχοι, καὶ τούτους ἐκέλευσεν Ἕλληνας στρατιώτας λαμβάνειν, πολλοὺς καὶ ἀγαθούς.»

inference_aids.gloss: φρούραρχος: ὃς τῶν ἐν τῇ πόλει στρατιωτῶν ἄρχει

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Καὶ οἱ φρούραρχοι ἐπείθοντο;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος.
segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Ἐπείθοντο· οἱ γὰρ φρούραρχοι τοῦ Κύρου ἦσαν,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Διὰ τί δὲ Ἕλληνας;» ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος· «ὁ γὰρ βασιλεὺς ὑποπτεύσει.»

pins.note: Future indicative, not aorist subjunctive.

segments.speaker: char-diodoros

segments.text: «Πρόφασιν εἶχεν,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν· «ἔλεγε γὰρ ὅτι ὁ Τισσαφέρνης ταῖς πόλεσιν ἐπιβουλεύοι.»

inference_aids.gloss: πρόφασις: λόγος ὃν λέγει τις ἀντὶ τοῦ ἀληθοῦς

pins.note: Oblique optative.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Αἱ γὰρ τῶν Ἑλλήνων πόλεις αἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ πρότερον τοῦ Τισσαφέρνους ἦσαν,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.
segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τότε δὲ πᾶσαι ἀπέστησαν πρὸς τὸν Κῦρον, πλὴν Μιλήτου.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἀφίστασθαι ↔ πείθεσθαι: οὐκέτι τῷ Τισσαφέρνει ἐπείθοντο

pins.note: Intransitive root aorist: revolted; not transitive first aorist. Morpheus also indexes under ἀφεστήξω.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐν δὲ Μιλήτῳ ὁ Τισσαφέρνης ᾔσθετο ὅτι καὶ οἱ Μιλήσιοι ἀφίστασθαι βούλονται.»

pins.note: Morpheus anomalous index ἀφεστήξω; canonical grc-aphistemi ἀφίστημι; present middle infinitive revolt.

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Τοὺς μὲν οὖν ἀπέκτεινε, τοὺς δὲ ἐξέβαλεν.»

inference_aids.gloss: ἐξέβαλεν ← ἐκβάλλω (ἐκ + ἔβαλον): ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἤλασεν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ἐξέβαλεν;» ἔφη ὁ Γρύλλος· «τοῦτο μὲν ἀληθῶς ἔβαλεν.»
segments.speaker: char-gryllos

segments.text: «Οἱ δὲ ἐκβληθέντες φυγάδες ἦσαν, καὶ πρὸς τὸν Κῦρον ἔφυγον,» ἔφη ὁ Ξενοφῶν.

inference_aids.gloss: φυγάς ← φεύγω: ὃς ἐκ τῆς πατρίδος ἐξεβλήθη

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

segments.text: «Ὁ δὲ Κῦρος στράτευμα ἤθροισε καὶ τὴν Μίλητον ἐπολιόρκει, ὅπως τοὺς φυγάδας κατάγοι.»

inference_aids.gloss: πολιορκεῖν: στρατὸν περὶ τὴν πόλιν ἔχειν, ὅπως αὐτὴν λάβῃ
κατάγειν τοὺς φυγάδας ↔ ἐκβάλλειν: πάλιν οἴκαδε ἄγειν

segments.speaker: char-xenophon

grammar.note_en:
Many Greek verbs have a first aorist marked by σ (ἐπεβούλευ-σ-εν, ἤθροι-σ-ε), sometimes with changes to the stem, so not every one is simply the present stem plus -σα-. A large group of very common verbs does something else: the aorist uses a different, usually shorter, stem and puts on it the same endings as the imperfect (-ον, -ες, -ε(ν), -ομεν, -ετε, -ον; middle -όμην, -ου, -ετο). This is the second aorist. It means exactly what any aorist means; only the way it is built differs. For reading, the skill is to go from the form you meet to the word you would look up.

The narrow point of this chapter is the difference between such an aorist and the imperfect of the same verb, because their endings are identical and only the stem tells them apart. Sosias says Tissaphernes ἀεὶ πάντας διέβαλλεν (s030), ‘was always slandering everyone’: two λ, the present stem βαλλ-, an imperfect, a habit. Xenophon says ὁ Τισσαφέρνης τὸν Κῦρον … διέβαλεν (s027), ‘Tissaphernes slandered Cyrus’: one λ, the aorist stem βαλ-, one act. Gryllus hears the same stem inside διέβαλεν and asks τί ἔβαλεν; ἀκόντιον; (s028), and later, when Tissaphernes throws the Milesians out, ἐξέβαλεν, he is satisfied: τοῦτο μὲν ἀληθῶς ἔβαλεν (s076).

To find the dictionary word, work in three steps. First take off the augment; in a compound it stands after the preverb, so look inside: δι-έ-βαλεν, ἐξ-έ-βαλεν, συν-έ-λαβεν, κατ-ή-γαγεν. Second, take off the ending to see the stem: βαλ-, λαβ-, ἀγαγ-. Third, recognise the present you already know that belongs with this stem. The patterns below are clues for recognising a pair you have met, not rules that generate the dictionary form: the present is usually the longer form; it doubles a consonant (βαλ- → βάλλω), adds a nasal or -αν- (λαβ- → λαμβάνω, αἰσθ- → αἰσθάνομαι), has a fuller vowel (φυγ- → φεύγω), adds -σκ- (παθ- → πάσχω, where θ + σκ became σχ), or doubles its first syllable (γεν- → γίγνομαι). A few verbs work the other way round: the aorist doubles (ἀγαγ- beside ἄγω). And a few use a different word altogether, which has to be learned as a pair: εἶδον belongs to ὁράω, ἦλθον to ἔρχομαι, εἶπον to λέγω.

Outside the indicative there is no augment, so the bare stem shows: in the active the infinitive ends in an accented -εῖν, and the masculine nominative singular participle in an accented -ών (middle: -έσθαι, -όμενος). Cyrus’s pretext ὡς Πισίδας βουλόμενος ἐκβαλεῖν (s116) is the aorist infinitive of ἐκβάλλω (one λ, accent on the ending); the present infinitive would be ἐκβάλλειν. In Xenophon’s own text λαβὼν Τισσαφέρνην (s125) is the aorist participle of λαμβάνω, ‘taking’; the present participle would be λαμβάνων. The same passage has ἀνέβη (from ἀναβαίνω) and κατέστη (from καθίστημι), root aorists: the personal ending is added straight to the root, without the connecting vowel ο/ε; recognise them, but they are not yet asked for.

You are not asked to make second aorists. When you meet one, strip the augment and the ending, find the stem, and ask which present you know it belongs to; the table lists every one in this chapter.

parergon.title: ὡς in Xenophon’s first paragraph
parergon.body_en: Xenophon’s opening sentences use ὡς three times, and the pretext in the hook adds a fourth. With a noun, ὡς means ‘as’: λαβὼν Τισσαφέρνην ὡς φίλον (s125), ‘taking Tissaphernes as a friend’. With a verb of saying it means ‘that’: διαβάλλει … ὡς ἐπιβουλεύοι αὐτῷ (s126), ‘slanders him (saying) that he was plotting’. With a participle it gives a reason or aim as the subject sees it: ὡς ἀποκτενῶν (s127), ‘meaning to kill him’; ὡς Πισίδας βουλόμενος ἐκβαλεῖν (s116), ‘as if wanting to drive out the Pisidians’. ὡς marks the claim, not the fact. Κεφ. 33 and 35 return to these uses.

pair.sense_grc: διαβάλλω τινὰ πρός τινα, διέβαλον: ψευδῆ περί τινος λέγω · «Ὁ δὲ Τισσαφέρνης τὸν Κῦρον πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν διέβαλεν»
pair.sense_en: slander, accuse falsely (+ accusative of the person; πρός + accusative of the hearer)

pair.sense_grc: ἐκβάλλω τινά, ἐξέβαλον: ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἐλαύνω · «τοὺς δὲ ἐξέβαλεν»

families.spelling_note: Both are βάλλω ‘throw’ with a preverb, and the augment goes after the preverb: δι-έ-βαλεν (s027), ἐξ-έ-βαλεν (s075). Δια- loses its α before the augment, and ἐκ- becomes ἐξ- before any vowel (ἐκ- → ἐξ-έβαλεν). The aorist passive has the stem βλη-: διεβλήθη, οἱ ἐκβληθέντες. Ἐκβάλλω is the sum of its parts: to throw someone out, as Tissaphernes threw the Milesians out of their city, so that Gryllus can say τοῦτο μὲν ἀληθῶς ἔβαλεν (s076). Διαβάλλω is not: ‘to throw across’ came to mean to set people at odds by what one says about them, and so ‘to slander’. Nothing is thrown, which is Gryllus’s mistake (τί ἔβαλεν; ἀκόντιον; s028); the person slandered is in the accusative and the hearer takes πρός + accusative (πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφόν).

notes: Apparatus by GPT-6.1-Sol (cx 1115-131922-8462), verified and edited by Claude Opus 5.5: protected story text, IDs, section titles, inference-aid wording, grammar, families and media briefs were Claude's. No audio or generated raster art (one cover attempt returned OpenRouter HTTP 402).

P009 k=6: eighteen vocabulary items, 4/5/4/5. x1 takes the first four stage-2 words; x2 the first two stage-1 words, remaining two stage-2 words and first stage-3 word; x3 the next two stage-1 and next two stage-3 words; x4 the remaining two stage-1 and three stage-3 words. Order is preserved within every stage. All evidence is read before its exercise; stage-2 citations point to chapter24. Later-section evidence makes stage1 grc-astheneo appear last although its s018 evidence is early. Stage1 grc-epibouleuo uses s042, avoiding the defining s029 gloss; grc-athroizo uses s078. Two-option sets are allowed by COURSE.md and owner brief.

Second aorists are recognition only: no exercise answer or production-card cloze answer is a second-aorist form, infinitive, participle, subjunctive or optative. No production source is a preview or receptive segment. grc-diaballo card uses imperfect διέβαλλεν s030; grc-katago uses present κατάγειν s080.

All exact items accept movable nu and contracted/uncontracted variants as applicable. Eight new answer-only analytical expansions are appended to plan/accepted-forms.json with reasons. Existing ᾐτιάετο adjudication stands. x4-4 admits completed healing or ongoing care and therefore accepts ἐθεράπευσε(ν)/ἐθεράπευε(ν), with the imperfect cell already read in chapter24 s003. x4-5 likewise admits aorist or imperfect ὕβρισε(ν)/ὕβριζε(ν).

εὐηργέτει s064 is keyed first because it is the story spelling; εὐεργέτει is also accepted. LSJ εὐεργετέω records εὐηργ- in X.Ap.26; Xenophon Ages.4.4 has εὐεργέτει. Sources: https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n43836/ and https://beta.perseus.tufts.edu/urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0032.tlg009.perseus-grc2:4/ . Analytical expansions are answer-policy variants, not claims of idiomatic uncontracted prose.

Nineteen genuinely new course lexemes, all used at least three times (3–6 uses). All ten row-production lexemes have exact anchored non-receptive clozes. Genuine new core encounters: only τάσσω (three uses) and ἀνά (two uses), below advisory core_encountered_budget [5,10]; protected prose unchanged. ἀνά is a function preposition rather than a content word. Planned τέσσαρες is earlier: chapter18 s098 τέτταρας. τέταρτος already dates to l21 (τετάρτῃ s075), also chapter23 s105 Τέταρτον, so is not new. θάνατος already occurs chapter19 s078 θάνατον. Retrospective core entries preserve those earlier dates rather than declare new encounters.

Other suspected first-core words are earlier: μύριοι l20; πέμπτος l18; δεύτερος l03; γνώμη l20; ὁμολογέω l11; βάρβαρος l18; πειράω/πειράομαι l17; ψευδής l20; δοῦλος/δίκαιος/γείτων l12; ταχύ under ταχύς l11. No duplicate IDs are declared for them.

All nineteen recall_must words occur in the prose. Used recall_due are μήποτε, διαλλάττω and ὀργίζομαι. Unused recall_due: grc-phthoneo, grc-hippazomai, grc-syntheke, grc-koinoneo, grc-aideomai, grc-apallasso, grc-kalamos, grc-praos, grc-symphero, grc-pistis. Only μισθός of recall_may is read; συμβουλεύω appears in an exercise but is not claimed as prose recall. Additional ξένος and stage-3 words are genuinely recycled.

The reading has 1,399 running words, within the advisory 1,200–1,400 window, including the approximately 110-word authentic paragraph (plan count 111). metrics.sentences=128 follows the checker’s segment convention. There are 37 margin glosses. Raster cover, scene and vignette remain briefs only; no absent image is needed for inference.

The adjacent repetition Ὁ χειμὼν χειμὼν ἦν s005 is deliberate subject/predicate and the promised reply from chapter24 s043. The 14 duplicate-sentence warnings are repeated speech tags ἤρετο ὁ Διόδωρος, deliberately naming the speaker (NOTES). The 9 attic-tt warnings are Τισσαφέρνης/Τισσαφέρνην/Τισσαφέρνους, a name’s established spelling, as in chapter24. The 29 construction-unlicensed warnings are the known checker mismatch for already licensed named constructions; tags remain unchanged.

Two deterministic SVG margin diagrams are wired: the family tree (560×500, s026, moved there from s014 on review so that its βασιλεύς label does not anticipate the story) and the first march map (720×405, s116), drawn by Claude from Natural Earth 1:50m land polygons (public domain) in an equirectangular projection centred on 38°N; it covers Sardis to Cilicia as the plan row asks and labels places already read (Σάρδεις, Ἔφεσος, Μίλητος, Χερρόνησος, Πισίδαι, θάλαττα, Ἀσία) plus Κιλικία, the march's next goal (added to the course names; extended east after the confirming re-check, which had found the first version stopping short of Cilicia). Later units draw the route. Both rendered with librsvg and inspected: no overlap; label sizes pass the checker's 14 px rule at 256 px width.

Morpheus was run in accented Attic mode on all story prose and all authored Greek apparatus, including options, hints, accepted answers, lexicon fronts, SVG labels, grammar/families and margin glosses. Pins select analyzer-compatible readings while notes and popup leaves give canonical/contextual morphology. θεῷ is contextually feminine despite the analyzer’s masculine-only entry; εὔνους s064/s066 is accusative plural. ἀφίστασθαι is canonical ἀφίστημι despite Morpheus’s ἀφεστήξω index. Πισίδαι is retained as supplied: Morpheus proposes Πίσιδαι, but primary Arrian Anab.1.28.1–2 displays Πισίδαι; this alone does not justify correcting the source spelling.

Margin-gloss licensing audited separately because check.mjs does not cover it: 241 Greek word tokens checked. Every defining word has a core/course/name/function or earlier licence. Four apparent registry misses are authentic self-headwords covered only at their own anchors: ἀπέδειξε s124; πεδίον in Καστωλοῦ πεδίον s124; τριακόσιοι (=300) s125; βασιλείαν in the s126 kingship phrase. They are locally glossed receptive material, not newly global productive words. New ἐξαιτεῖσθαι and earlier μεταπέμπεται are explicitly registered surface forms. No protected margin wording was changed.

Continuity is a new unmerged chapter delta. The continuity warning requests merger into the cumulative ledger; that is deliberately left to the owner’s integration workflow, within the apparatus-only boundary. No cumulative lexicon/continuity merge was run. Independent exercise review found no blockers; whole-chapter independent review remains required before finalize.

Independent review cx 1115-133707-3794 (GPT-6.1-Sol): blockers fixed by Claude. B1 s067 τούτοις → τούτους ἐκέλευσεν (κελεύω + acc. + inf.). B2 s123 ἧς is an ordinary genitive with σατράπην ("satrap of which"), not relative attraction; gloss and popup corrected (the plan row's exception text still says attraction: recorded in OPEN.md for the planner). B3 Μάθημα: first aorists described as σ-marked, not "present stem + σα"; -εῖν/-ών specified as active and masc. nom. sg. with middle -έσθαι/-όμενος; root aorists defined as having no connecting vowel, ἀνέβη ← ἀναβαίνω; "rebuild the present" recast as recognising a known pair. B4 the march map is now delivered (above). Suggestions taken: s038 "all the Persians" → «πάντες οἱ παρόντες»; stemma anchor moved; cover brief no longer crowns Artaxerxes before Darius dies. Speech tags kept: NOTES require naming each changed speaker. Confirming re-check cx 1115-135047-31910: B1–B3 resolved, no new errors; B4 was then completed by extending the map to Cilicia.

review_questions.question: [?] s001: the messenger leaves on the third day counted inclusively from his arrival in chapter23 (evening=day1). Confirm that this is the intended elapsed interval; no exact calendar date is introduced.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: inclusive counting from Κεφ. 23 fits Κεφ. 24's prediction.

review_questions.question: [?] s030: Sosias calls Tissaphernes ungrateful and always slandering everyone. This is his opinion, not a sourced historical generalisation. Retain as character judgment only.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted as Sosias's opinion, logged as such.

review_questions.question: [?] s038: Cyrus is arrested like a slave before all the Persians. Anab.1.1.3–4 says arrested and dishonoured; the comparison and audience are dramatization. Confirm, or suggest replacing with the source-bounded arrest/dishonour statement.
review_questions.resolution: Revised on review: «καὶ πάντες οἱ παρόντες τοῦτο εἶδον»; the slave comparison remains marked dramatization (Anab. 1.1.3–4: arrest and dishonour).

review_questions.question: [?] s063: he shared his intention with few. Consistent with Anab.3.1.10, not further evidence about the identities or exact knowledge of those few. Confirm the limited reconstruction.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted as a labelled inference consistent with Anab. 3.1.10 (only Clearchus among the Greeks knew); it does add a knowledge claim (Cyrus confided in few), which the continuity log now says.

review_questions.question: [?] s066: Sosias says he won us with kindnesses. His personal inclusion is invented testimony. Confirm without resolving his later recruitment/service plant.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted as invented testimony; Sosias's unit and recruitment route stay unresolved for Κεφ. 26.

review_questions.question: [?] s098: to besiege Miletus with the exiles simplifies Anab.1.1.11, as if to make war on Tissaphernes with the Milesian exiles. Confirm the simplification, or suggest the source’s broader objective in a writer revision.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted as a contextual simplification of Anab. 1.1.11, reconstruction label kept.

review_questions.question: [?] s103–s109: a daric apiece leaves the pay period implicit. Anab.1.3.21 implies a daric per month, raised to one and a half. The per-day question and horse-tending counterfactual are household invention. Confirm that readers infer a question/joke, not a historical daily wage.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: the counterfactual rejects a daily wage; Anab. 1.3.21 gives a daric a month.

review_questions.question: [?] s116: the hook quotes Anab.1.2.1 in Xenophon’s mouth and is marked receptive because of ὡς + participle (G33). Confirm the oral retelling/quotation boundary and preserve its exclusion from production sources.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: oral quotation of Anab. 1.2.1, receptive and excluded from production. Scope note: the row's G33 exception names the authentic span ὡς ἀποκτενῶν; this hook span is licensed only by the row's fixed hook line, not as general permission for G33 in prose.

review_questions.question: [?] s124: retain Marchant’s ἁθροίζονται with rough breathing beside the frame’s smooth ἀθροίζω forms. Pin and contextual popup identify the same lexeme; no orthographic normalisation of the authentic source.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: Marchant prints ἁθροίζονται; kept.

review_questions.question: [?] s107–s108: only two genuine first-core lexemes rather than planned 5–10, and ἀνά occurs only twice. Reported without changing protected prose; decide whether the function-word recurrence is acceptable.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: earlier encounters explain the low first-use count; no padding.

review_questions.question: [?] s116 margin: Morpheus suggests Πίσιδαι for the supplied Πισίδαι; a primary Arrian text also displays Πισίδαι, so no correction follows from the analyzer. Confirm the chosen name authority if standardising across the course.
review_questions.resolution: Review accepted: Πισίδαι as printed (Arrian 1.28); the analyser does not overrule the edition.
